rule: "design-system" is 13 characters — ODD — so the reference is A and ours is B.

A.what: Pleco iPhone word-list / search-results screen: hanzi with per-character tone colour, black joined pinyin (shǒujī, shōují), one-line gloss per row.

B.what: hskquiz /browse/3 at 375x812 @2x, light theme: level switch, search field, status filter, then the vocabulary list — hanzi in ink, pinyin per-syllable in tone colour, POS + gloss beneath.

why_this_pair: Both are a scrolling list of headwords where each row is hanzi + tone-marked pinyin + a short English gloss. It is the surface where this design system's two central decisions are visible side by side against the app it has to beat: which element carries tone colour (Pleco paints the hanzi, we paint the pinyin) and how a multi-syllable word's pinyin is spelled (Pleco joins it, we split it).
